content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Columbus

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's education and hours-worked prerequisites to verify you meet the baseline. Granite PM Academy's advisors can walk you through eligibility questions before you enroll.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours
steps_items.text: Attend Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Boot Camp. Our Columbus cohorts run on a fixed schedule, delivered by experienced practitioners. You'll cover the PMBOK Guide framework, exam domains, and real-world scenarios—all in a structured classroom environment.

steps_items.heading: Submit Application & Fee
steps_items.text: After finishing your 35 contact hours, submit your PMI application with proof of education and experience. Pay PMI's exam fee directly to PMI. Granite PM Academy will provide your certificate of completion to support your application.

steps_items.heading: Prepare & Sit for Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and review sessions—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your exam through PMI's testing partner. You'll sit for the computer-based exam at an authorized test center.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: PMP credentials renew on a three-year cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, volunteering, or project work. Granite PM Academy offers ongoing PDU-eligible courses to support your continuous learning and credential renewal.

fq_items.question: What’s the difference between the PMP Bootcamp and PMP Certification Training?

fq_items.question: Does the bootcamp satisfy PMI’s 35 contact hour requirement?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our PMP Bootcamp includes the full 35 PMI contact hours required to apply for the PMP exam. You’ll receive a certificate of completion immediately after the course.

fq_items.answer: Yes. Large Columbus employers in insurance (Nationwide, Huntington), healthcare (OhioHealth, Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center), and financial services actively seek PMP-certified professionals and list the credential as preferred in job postings. The metro area's steady demand for experienced project managers, driven by corporate expansions and technology investment, makes certification a competitive advantage that typically supports stronger compensation and advancement opportunities.

fq_items.answer: Insurance, financial services, and healthcare organizations in Columbus—including Nationwide Mutual, JPMorgan Chase, Cardinal Health, and OhioHealth—most consistently seek PMP-certified candidates. Battelle Memorial Institute and American Electric Power similarly value certified project managers. These sectors dominate Columbus hiring and offer competitive packages for certified professionals.

fq_items.answer: Yes. The live-virtual format allows you to join from your office, home, or any location with reliable internet—no need to travel to an in-person classroom. fq_items.question: Should Columbus professionals pursue PMP or CAPM certification first?
fq_items.answer: If you lack the required project management experience, CAPM is a strategic entry point that demonstrates foundational knowledge and helps you build toward PMP eligibility while working in Columbus's competitive job market. Employers in insurance, healthcare, and finance recognize CAPM as credible preparation. Once you meet PMP prerequisites through full-time roles at major local employers, the boot camp accelerates your path to the higher credential and stronger earning potential.
